_comment: Colour slide films from the makers' product information bulletins, read off the vector graphs (pdf.js; axes from the grid lines, the tick values read off the rendered page). char: Status A density per layer (R = red-sensitive / cyan dye, G / magenta, B / yellow) vs log10 exposure in lux-seconds, daylight. sens: log10 relative spectral sensitivity per layer (1/exposure for a density 1.0 above D-min), drawn by the maker down to about -0.7. dye: spectral diffuse density of each dye, each normalised to a peak of 1. negatives: colour negative films (Status M curves, sensitivities, the published D-min and midscale-neutral spectra; the three dyes' shapes, which Kodak doesn't publish for still films, from a sister motion-picture negative, checked against the film's own neutral spectrum). papers: colour printing papers (Status A curves, log sensitivities, the three dyes in reflection).

Fujifilm FUJICHROME Velvia 50 Professional [RVP50], product information bulletin AF3-0221E2, p. 8: characteristic curves (Status A, daylight 1/50 s, absolute log H in lux-seconds) and spectral sensitivities traced from the embedded 1-bit raster figures at their native resolution (1896x1702 and 1843x1684); the axes are calibrated from the printed grid lines and tick labels (-3.0...1.0 by 0.5, 0...4.0 by 0.5; worst grid residual 0.006 log H / 0.007 D). The three lines are distinguished by the sheet's own style (R solid, G long dash, B short dash): the solid red curve is traced to the toe, and G/B are measured where their ink separates from it and interpolated smoothly where it merges (marked on the overlay). The spectral-dye curves cross; they are separated by iterative assignment to the nearest ink of smooth single-peak models fixed at the labelled 440/540/650 nm maxima. Process E-6/CR-56.

Fujifilm FUJICHROME PROVIA 100F Professional [RDP III], data sheet AF3-036E, p. 6: characteristic curves (Status A, daylight 1/50 s, absolute log H in lux-seconds), spectral sensitivities and spectral-dye-density curves. The characteristic and dye figures are four separations each (a K plate with the grid and text plus one 1-bit plate per curve); each curve is traced from its own plate at native resolution (1004x886 and 972x734). The sensitivity curves are vector. The x-axis frame is log H -3.5: the printed labels -3.0, -2.0, -1.0, 0.0 and 1.0 sit on the five even grid lines (measured label centres 218.5, 405.5, 592.0, 779.5, 963.5 px on the K plate), so task 69's reading of the left frame as -3.0 put every log H 0.5 decade high; task 70 re-corrected the axis. The dashed characteristic curves are drawn only where they separate from the solid red line; below those points they are extended along the common solid ink (G from log H -1.5, B from -2.2) and the extension is marked. Process E-6/CR-56.

Fujifilm FUJICHROME Sensia 100 [RA], data sheet AF3-091E, p. 5: characteristic curves (Status A, daylight 1/50 s, absolute log H in lux-seconds), spectral sensitivities and spectral-dye-density curves, all traced from the embedded 1-bit raster figures at native resolution (938x853, 932x841, 935x703). Axes from the printed grid and tick labels (x -3.5...1.0 by 0.5, y 0...4.0 by 0.5; worst grid residual 0.011 log H / 0.013 D). The solid red characteristic curve is traced across the sheet; G/B are measured where their ink separates and interpolated where it merges, as marked. The crossing dye curves are separated by the same iterative nearest-ink method as Velvia 50. Process E-6/CR-56.

Fujifilm FUJICHROME 64T TYPE II Professional [RTPII], data sheet AF3-024E, p. 6: characteristic curves (Status A, tungsten, absolute log H in lux-seconds) and spectral sensitivities, each from four 1-bit separation plates at native resolution (969x868, 989x852); the spectral-dye curves are vector. The dashed characteristic curves are drawn only where they separate from the solid red line and are extended along it below those points, marked on the overlay. Tungsten-balanced 3200 K; modelled and rendered as shot under its own light, as T64 is. Process E-6/CR-56.

Fujifilm FUJICHROME Sensia 200 [RM], data sheet AF3-080E, p. 5: characteristic curves (Status A, daylight 1/50 s, absolute log H in lux-seconds) and spectral sensitivities from the vector figure, its fragments joined in order into one monotone curve per layer at 0.05 decade / 5 nm. The x-axis is read from the printed labels: -3.0, -2.0, -1.0 and 0.0 sit on the interior grid lines (label centres 646, 928, 1209.5 and 1509 px on a 400 dpi render; lines at 651.5, 939.5, 1219.5 and 1505 px), every other of the nine lines, so the plot box is log H -3.5 ... +0.5 and the curves run -3.5 ... 0.0, inside it. Task 69's proxy xr=(-3.16, 0.03) compressed the axis and shifted it; task 71 re-corrected it from the labels. The dye figure is a raster; the dyes are borrowed from the same-generation Fujichrome set printed by Velvia 100 / Astia 100F / Provia 400X. Registered by the density alignment at the ISO mid-grey (shift R +0.020, B +0.045). Process E-6/CR-56.

Fujifilm FUJICHROME Sensia 400 [RH], data sheet AF3-081E, p. 5: characteristic curves (Status A, daylight 1/50 s, absolute log H in lux-seconds) and spectral sensitivities from the vector figure, joined into one monotone curve per layer; the blue curve is drawn only where it separates from green, so its shared left stem is extended along the green ink to the frame and marked. The x-axis frame is log H -4.0 ... 0.0: the printed labels -4.0, -3.0, -2.0, -1.0 and 0.0 sit on the frame and every other grid line (measured label centres 519, 800.5, 1082, 1364, 1663 px on the 400 dpi render), with grid lines every 0.5 decade. Task 69 read the frame as -3.16 ... 0.03, which compressed the whole axis by 3.19/4.0 and shifted it; task 70 re-corrected it. The dye figure is a raster; the dyes are borrowed from the same-generation Fujichrome set (Velvia 100 / Astia 100F / Provia 400X). Registered by the density alignment at the ISO mid-grey (shift R +0.020, B 0). Process E-6/CR-56.

Kodak EKTACHROME Professional Infrared EIR Film, publication TI-2323 (Sept 2005), p. 7 characteristic curves and spectral sensitivities and p. 8 spectral-dye-density curves, all vector. False colour: the yellow-forming layer is green-sensitive (B read), the magenta-forming layer red-sensitive (G read) and the cyan-forming layer infrared-sensitive (R read); the film is shot through a Wratten 12 yellow filter, applied to the visible sensitivities. APPROXIMATION: a normal X3F carries no infrared channel, so the IR layer's exposure is estimated from a scale-invariant vegetation index on the white-balanced camera layers: vi = (G - (R+B)/2) / (R+G+B) with low B/G marks foliage, which gets a plant-like 0.45 NIR reflectance independent of visible brightness, so a dark conifer goes red/magenta; a blue-dominant sky gets almost no IR and stays blue; lit non-vegetation (skin, paint, soil) tends to a 0.30 NIR reflectance through a smooth 0.02..0.10 luminance ramp (not a threshold), so deep shadow and dark hair keep their own luminance and do not posterise. The curves are registered to the ISO mid-grey (shift R -0.76, G -0.65, B -0.97 decade; the sheet prints no absolute exposure scale on this figure). This is a false-colour approximation, flagged in /api/films; it is not a measurement of infrared.

negatives.src: Fujifilm FUJICOLOR PRO 400H PROFESSIONAL, data sheet AF3-176E, p. 8: characteristic curves (Status M, daylight), spectral sensitivities, D-min and mid-scale-neutral spectra. Fuji's fourth, cyan-sensitive layer (it holds back the red-sensitive layer) is not modelled. The sheet plots the characteristic curves on a relative log H scale: its ISO speed point (Status M green at D-min + 0.15) is 0.26 decades right of the same-ISO Kodak control sheet. The digitised x values were re-registered left by 0.26 decades so the stored axis is absolute (REPORT-64).
